body.statement: For every \(I\in\mathfrak J_2^{\mathrm{nw}}\), if every nontrivial variable in \(V\) is binary and \(g\) uses \(\ell\ge1\) original response blocks, then exact sharp endpoints and rational attaining finite SCMs are computable without a width assumption in \(B^{O(\ell(1+\log B)^2)}\) bit operations. The algorithm enumerates supports only through the exact raw rank of each relevant block and obtains one rational feasible point for every irrelevant block.
body.justification: This gives a second exact regime when a useful decomposition is unavailable but the query touches few original roots.
body.gap: Arroyo et al. obtain polynomial-cardinality column generation for one intervention; the proposed logarithmic-square rank bound covers several explicitly represented relevant blocks and an objective of degree at least three.
body.consumer: A canonical optimizer can dispatch sparse-block binary queries even when its measured scalar response width is large.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(I\in\mathfrak J_2^{\mathrm{nw}}\), and remove singleton observed arguments from each response table.  Consider first a root block with two nontrivial binary children.  Let \(d_1,d_2\) be the numbers of binary observed arguments of their structural response functions and put
\[
h_j=2^{d_j}\quad(j=1,2),\qquad
N_c:=|R_c|=2^{h_1+h_2}. \tag{35}
\]
There are at most \(2^{d_1+d_2}=h_1h_2\) external-parent contexts; shared parents or a parent edge between the two children only decreases this count.  Each context has at most four binary output rows.  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{rank}(A_c)
\le4h_1h_2
\le(h_1+h_2)^2
=(\log_2N_c)^2, \tag{36}
\]
where the middle inequality is \((h_1-h_2)^2\ge0\).  For a block with one nontrivial child, if \(h=2^d\), then \(N_c=2^h\), there are at most \(h\) contexts and two output rows per context, whence
\[
\operatorname{rank}(A_c)\le2h=2\log_2N_c. \tag{37}
\]
Blocks with no nontrivial child have constant size and rank.  Thus, uniformly,
\[
r_c:=\operatorname{rank}(A_c)
\le4(1+\log_2N_c)^2. \tag{38}
\]

By the \(K_c\) version of \(\text{lem:rational-factor-vertices}\), every vertex has positive support of size at most \(r_c\), and enumerating all supports through that exact rank lists every vertex.  The number of tested supports is bounded by
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{r_c}\binom{N_c}{j}
\le(N_c+1)^{r_c+1}. \tag{39}
\]
Because \(\text{ass:complete-response-list}\) lists every coordinate, \(N_c\le B\).  Equations (38)--(39) consequently bound the complete vertex list of one relevant block by
\[
B^{O((1+\log B)^2)}. \tag{40}
\]

The objective is affine in each original block by \(\text{ass:block-affine-query}\).  The factor-replacement argument used in \(\text{thm:equality-factor-gluing}\), now applied directly to the compact product \(\prod_cK_c\), proves that its extrema occur at vertices of every relevant block.  Enumerate the Cartesian product of the vertex lists only for the \(\ell\) blocks occurring in a monomial of \(g\), and evaluate the explicit polynomial on each tuple.  The number of tuples is, by (40),
\[
B^{O(\ell(1+\log B)^2)}. \tag{41}
\]
For each irrelevant block, scan supports in increasing size up to its exact rank and stop at the first nonnegative consistent solution.  Nonemptiness from \(\text{lem:rational-h-representations}\) and the vertex criterion guarantee that the scan succeeds.  Its cost per block is bounded by (40), but these scans are added, not multiplied; there are at most \(B\) blocks.  Since \(\ell\ge1\), their total \(B^{O((1+\log B)^2)}\) cost is absorbed by (41).  The selected point is rational with \(O(B^2)\)-bit coordinates by \(\text{lem:rational-factor-vertices}\).

Exact evaluation of each serialized monomial and comparison of rational candidates has polynomial bit cost by (19).  Therefore (41) is a bit-operation bound, not merely an arithmetic-operation bound.  Concatenating an optimizing relevant tuple with the selected irrelevant vectors gives two rational points of \(\prod_cK_c\).  Finally, \(\text{prop:canonical-semantics}\) turns them into finite compatible SCMs and identifies their values with \(\underline\theta\) and \(\overline\theta\).  No width assumption or implicit response-column oracle was used.
